problems.quote: The accuracy score was calculated as the number of correct responses divided by the total number of problems attempted.
problems.note: The mechanical flag is valid: null is not an allowed measure value. However, the paper defines correct-answer accuracy without identifying its scoring procedure, and the supplied codebook has no explicit category for this measure. automated_score requires a creativity-scoring model; behavioral is defined as market or usage outcomes; neither is established here. Rater-based codes are also unconfirmed. This is an unresolved vocabulary conflict, not a numerical transcription error. printed is null because no supported replacement code can be confirmed. An explicit coding convention or allowance for unknown measurement methods is needed; assigning an unsupported category would violate the no-guess instruction.

problems.quote: LLMs (irrespective of their level of randomness in the 0.1- 1.2 range) increase accuracy (on average, from 45 to 55%, p < .05).
problems.note: The mechanical flag is valid: null is not an allowed se_basis value. The paper prints a p-value but does not identify the test, observation unit, or handling of the three task rounds. Thus participant-level uncertainty, or any other listed independence unit, cannot be confirmed. not_reported is explicitly reserved for a contrast with no reported uncertainty and would misdescribe the printed p-value. This is an unresolved vocabulary conflict. printed is null because the uncertainty basis is unreported, not because the contrast lacks uncertainty. An explicit unknown-basis convention or permission for null is needed; no supported replacement is available from the paper.

summary: Read the complete markdown conversion, including references, and extracted text from all six PDF pages; no appendix is present. Recovered Tables II and III with pymupdf.find_tables and inspected Figure 1. Checked all 11 requested slugs: ten are now correctly listed in not_extracted because their AUT, DAT, or individual-arm RAT analyses adjust for actual AI use and task duration, which rule 5 excludes. The defended AUT maximum-distance values and their table columns are correct; the NoAI coefficient is NoAI minus Low. DAT coefficients are explicitly omitted, so no numerical replacements can be transcribed. The retained pooled RAT contrast correctly reports 55% with AI versus 45% without AI, p < .05, before the separate actual-user subgroup results. Its arms, question, convergent construct, direction, immediate timing, AI availability, comparison type, and between-person status agree with the paper. Comparison-specific counts and the analysis unit are not established, so their null values are justified; Table I cell counts are not substituted for accuracy-analysis counts. No additional in-scope outcome or reported full-sample contrast is missing under rules 4-6. Two allowed-value failures remain for measure and se_basis. The paper and current codebook provide no defensible replacement for either; these are coding-vocabulary conflicts, not incorrect numerical values.
